The verb なる (to become / to turn into) takes this pattern, forming 'なるわけにはいかない' = 'I can't become / I can't allow myself to become.' The object of the transformation, 負け犬 ('loser dog,' i.e. a failure), is marked by に because なる uses に to indicate the result.

ops.issue: Two wrong readings: 父上 is read ちちうえ, not ちちじょう; and 何 before を is read なに (なん occurs only before だ/の/で/と/counters), so なんを is wrong.
Romaji reproduces the wrong readings from kana ('chichijou' for 父上, 'nano' for なんを); should reflect ちちうえ / なにを.
The honorific suffix 上 in 父上 is read うえ (ちちうえ), never じょう in this word.
何 directly before the object particle を is read なに; なん is used only before だ/の/で/と or counters.

before.jp: 父上、何をしておられるのか。
before.kana: ちちじょう、なんをしておられるのか。

structure_explanation.en: Here the target 〜れる・られる appears in HONORIFIC use (sonkeigo), not as a pure passive: しておる ('to be doing', humble/literary) takes れる to respectfully elevate the subject (the father), resulting in しておられる ('is doing', respectful form). 父上 ('father', a reverent term of address) is the implicit subject, 何を is the interrogative object, and のか closes the question in a reflective/literary manner.

before.jp: 父は車の運転がとてもうまい。
before.kana: ちちわくるまのうんてんがとてもうまい。

structure_explanation.en: The topic is 父 ('my father'), marked by は. The grammatical subject is 車の運転 ('the driving of the car'), marked by が. The predicate is the adjective うまい ('skilled / good at'), intensified by the adverb とても ('very'). The structure 'X は Y が adjective' indicates what X is good at: literally 'as for my father, the driving is very good'.

O predicado é o adjetivo うまい ('hábil / bom em'), intensificado pelo advérbio とても ('muito'). A estrutura 'X は Y が adjetivo' indica em que X é bom: literalmente 'quanto ao pai, a condução é muito boa'.
